objective: Frozen side check (sub-goal B91's first step), run before the proof attempt of ticket A: at every eigenvalue with even k = 2c >= 4 for sides 16, 32 and 64, compute the reduction of the family to ker X_b with the monomial complement and with the complement containing k G Y^j (2j < k - 1), in two parametrizations (the family Zhat in l, and Z(a + au)/(1 + u) in u), and test (S1) every entry (i, j) with i + j odd vanishes modulo the parameter to the power 2k, and (S2) every entry with i + j even has only odd powers of the parameter below 2k. B91's strong form (the reduction at k = 2c is the parameter times the reductions at c and c - 1 with the parameter squared) predicts S1 and S2 for some of the four variants at every tested eigenvalue. Decision rule, frozen: if one variant passes at every tested eigenvalue, the epic considers the induction on k and says which route it takes and why; if every variant fails somewhere, B91's strong form is recorded as refuted (the halving of the leading matrix, proved, stands) and the epic proceeds with ticket A's co-distance induction. Disclosed before registration: at one eigenvalue (k = 6, side 32, a = alpha^23) the monomial-complement entry (0, 1) has valuation 10 < 12 in u, and valuations do not depend on the parametrization, so S1 already fails for that complement there.
status: Refuted 2026-11-10 (frozen test, pre-registered in f8e8b996c, run once before ticket A): at the 61 eigenvalues with even k >= 4 for sides 16 to 64 the reduction of the family to the eigenvectors has a nonzero entry mixing even and odd powers of Y below order 2k in every variant (two complements, two parametrizations), so sub-goal B91's strong form (the reduction at k = 2c splits into the parameter times those at c and c - 1 with the parameter squared) is refuted at these sides; the halving of the leading matrix stands. The epic took the co-distance route.
title: Does the reduction split when the index halves
